Maps and finding your way back

Two maps show the generated terrain. You can mark places, set a destination and search for biomes. Your own builds are not drawn on the maps, so save a place before you travel far.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 6 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Two maps

The compact map is a small north-up view in the top-right corner. It shows 128 m across, centred on you, and is on by default. The fullscreen map is 512 m across when it opens and zooms from 128 m to about 131 km. Compact map Fullscreen world map

Key or actionWhat it does
MShow or hide the compact map.
Shift + MOpen or close the fullscreen map. The compact map stays.
EscClose the fullscreen map.
M on the fullscreen mapClose it and hide the compact map.

To make the compact map turn with you, set Settings > Interface > Layout > Compact map heading to On. The way you face is then always at the top, and the N, E, S and W labels move round the edge. The fullscreen map always stays north-up.

Good to know. The maps show generated terrain only. Blocks you place or dig do not appear on them. The compact map is hidden while a panel is open and in clean view (F1).

Look around the fullscreen map

  1. Press Shift + M to open the map. It opens centred on you. When you play offline, the world pauses while it is open. On a server, the world keeps running.
  2. Scroll the mouse wheel over the map to zoom in or out.
  3. Drag with the left mouse button to look around. Dragging does not move you.
  4. Press BACK TO PLAYER in the side panel to centre the map on you again.

The readout under the map shows the X and Z position under the cursor and its distance from you. With the cursor off the map, it shows the map centre and your height. Player arrow on the map You are the grey arrow with a dark outline. It points the way you face.

N, E, S and W labels mark the edges. A scale bar sits in the lower-left corner, and a legend in the lower-right corner names the markers.

Mark places

  1. Open the fullscreen map.
  2. Right-click the spot you want. The game adds a pin named Marker 1, Marker 2 and so on, and sets it as your destination. On water, the pin stands on the surface.
  3. Right-click an existing pin to remove it.

Markers use the same 16-place limit as the Journal. Rename them in the Journal to give them a clear name. Pins show as small amber squares on both maps, with their names on the fullscreen map. Right-click map markers

Careful. Right-clicking a pin removes it, even a named Journal place. To undo, open the Journal and press Restore removed. Only the last place you removed can come back, and only until you leave the world. If the game says the Journal is full, remove a place first.

Save places in the Journal

  1. Press E, then click the Journal tab or press Tab until it shows. You can also click the Journal button on the fullscreen map.
  2. Click the Name or Note field and type. Press Enter to finish typing. A name holds up to 32 plain letters and a note up to 96; accented and non-Latin letters take more room.
  3. Click Pin this location to save the spot where you stand. It also becomes your destination. A blank name becomes Place 1, Place 2 and so on.
  4. Click a place to select it. This also makes it your destination and loads its name and note. Edit them and click Save selected note.

The Journal holds 16 places and lists each one with its distance from you. Use Prev and Next to page through them. Places are saved per world. Journal places and notes

  • Remove selected pin deletes the selected place.
  • Restore removed brings back the last place you removed, with its name and note.
  • Show on map opens the fullscreen map centred on the selected place, or on your home crate when no place is selected.

Set a destination

The destination is the place the maps and the screen point to. It can be a map marker, a Journal place or an expedition site. It is saved with the world. Destinations: map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker

  • On both maps it shows as an amber square with a +. When it is off the map, the square waits at the edge in its direction.
  • In the world it shows as an amber light column 320 m tall.
  • On screen it shows as a gold diamond with the name and distance. The diamond sticks to the screen edge when the place is out of view. It reads HERE within 3 m.
  • The Journal shows the distance to it under its buttons, for example To Camp: 120 m.

There is no clear button. Pick another place to change the destination, or remove the selected place to clear it, but only when that place is the destination. Removing another place keeps the destination. With no destination, the maps show your home crate as the + square instead, with no beacon or diamond. Home crate: establish, storage, repair, pack up

Find a biome or landmark

  1. Open the fullscreen map and click the search field on the left.
  2. Type a name, such as crystal, meteorite, caldera or lava tunnel. The list filters as you type.
  3. Press Enter, or click a result. The map centres on the first match, highlights the matching terrain in cyan and drops a pin with the distance and coordinates.
  4. Press FIND NEXT to search outward for another match at least about 1 km from the last one, or CLEAR to remove the pin and highlight.

The locator does not move you. Pan the map first if you want to search from another spot, because the search starts at the map centre. It only searches while the fullscreen map is open, out to about 131 km. NO MATCH IN SAMPLED AREA means it found nothing. Map locator: find biomes and landmarks

The list includes Volcano, Cliff island, Mountain range and all 92 biomes. A name marked * cannot appear in this world, because the world was made by an older version of the game.

Travel by map (Creative only)

In Creative you can jump to a place from the map. In Survival the map is a chart only.

  1. Click a spot on the fullscreen map without dragging. You land on clear dry ground within about 9 m of it, or on the water surface when there is none.
  2. Or click the COORDINATES (METRES) field, type X Z, or X Y Z for an exact height, and press Enter or TELEPORT. Spaces or commas both work, and values must be within ±1,000,000.

X Z always looks for a safe surface spot. An X Y Z spot must be free, or the game says Position blocked; try X Z instead. After the jump, the status line gives your new X, Y and Z and the biome. On a server, the server makes the jump and allows one trip a second.

Careful. Teleporting does not save where you came from, and there is no go back button. Save a Journal place before you jump. Leave the boat helm first. Click the map to travel (creative) Teleport by coordinates (creative)

In Survival, clicking the map only shows a reminder, and the button reads CREATIVE MODE ONLY. Zooming, dragging, the locator and markers still work, and the maps show the whole world, even places you have not visited. In a solo world, F4 switches to Creative. The map in survival (chart only, no fog of war)

Read your coordinates

The small readout under the compact map shows FPS, your X, Y and Z in metres and your biome. It is on each time you start the game. Turn it off in Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics > FPS and coordinates. It is hidden while a panel is open. Coordinates and biome readout

  • North is -Z and east is +X, so walking north makes Z smaller.
  • Write the numbers down before a long trip. They are the same numbers the coordinates field uses.

Turn on the HUD compass

The HUD compass is off by default. Turn it on in Settings > Interface > Layout > HUD compass. HUD compass

  • A strip at the top left, under the status line, shows N, E, S and W around the way you face.
  • Your saved places show on the strip as small amber marks while they are within 90 degrees of your facing.
  • A cyan triangle points to the nearest known landmark: an expedition site or your locator pin. The line below names it, gives its distance and counts your pins.
  • Like the rest of the HUD, it hides in clean view (F1) and while a panel is open.

Get back to a lost build

  1. Stand at the build and open the Journal. Type a name in the Name box, then press Pin this location.
  2. Before you travel far, select the place and press Show on map to check where it sits.
  3. To return, click the place in the Journal to make it your destination. Then follow the beacon, the on-screen diamond or the amber mark on the HUD compass.

The maps show terrain, not your builds. A destination pin is the way back when a build is hard to recognise in the terrain.
